clue.text: Girl having religious doubts? That's symptomatic

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
an agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known, so doubts religious claims

explanation.surface: A girl's crisis of faith is said to be a symptom of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the girl's doubts are only wordplay; the definition is 'symptomatic' after the link 'That's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnostic sign is one that indicates a particular illness, as a symptom does.

clue.text: As one worshipped by fans, I had nothing left

parts.note: 'd is the contracted form of had, as in I'd
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone with nothing left says they are adored by fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop star or film star adored by followers is commonly called an icon or object of worship.

clue.text: Ealing could be pleasant

indicators.note: suggests the letters of the word Ealing could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A remark that the London suburb of Ealing might be a nice place.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A genial person is friendly and cheerful, agreeable company.

clue.text: Survive as the batsman who is the tenth victim

definitions.meaning: to survive something is to live longer than it

definitions.text: the batsman who is the tenth victim
definitions.meaning: in cricket the tenth wicket ends an innings, so that batsman is the one dismissed at the end

explanation.surface: Lasting through as the final batsman dismissed in a cricket innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings ends when ten of the eleven batsmen are dismissed ('out'); the tenth victim is the one 'out last'.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlive or endure longer than something is to survive it; the cricketer is literally dismissed in final place.

clue.text: This left-winger is wrong on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror turns things round, so the word for wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A remark that, thinking about it, this leftist is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a far-left activist. 'On reflection' looks like 'after thinking', but turns TORT round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trot is a follower of Trotsky, a revolutionary socialist of the far left.

clue.text: See joy around the street

indicators.note: the word for joy goes around the abbreviation for street

parts.note: cheer is gladness or joy

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at happiness surrounding the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a bishop's diocese. Chester is a cathedral city and diocese in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district of a bishop, and Chester is the seat of one.

clue.text: A pinker drunk, unwell inside, gets the medicine

indicators.note: the word for unwell goes inside the rearranged letters
a drunk person is muddled, so the letters of a pinker are jumbled

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone more flushed from drink and feeling poorly takes some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges A PINKER into PAINKER, and 'inside' puts ILL into it after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic drug such as aspirin is a type of medicine that relieves pain.

clue.text: Being put at risk, finished harbouring indignation

indicators.note: to harbour is to hold within, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: ended means finished
anger is indignation or rage

explanation.surface: Danger looms because someone's outrage has come to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something threatened or in danger, such as a species facing extinction, is under threat.

clue.text: Murderer I put in prison

indicators.note: means the letter I is placed inside the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to locking up a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Cain killed his brother Abel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cain, son of Adam and Eve, is the first killer in the Bible.

clue.text: Various token words may be used by writer

indicators.note: suggests the letters of token words come in a varied arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer might employ a range of symbolic words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' looks like a description of words a writer chooses, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A downward movement of the pen in handwriting is one stroke that anyone writing makes.

clue.text: Colour when capital city is given new face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so the first letter of the city is swapped for another

parts.note: Vienna is the capital of Austria

explanation.surface: A colour appears when a capital city gets a facelift.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not clued; VIENNA with its V replaced makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt or raw sienna is an earthy brownish pigment used by painters.

clue.text: What Venus's flytrap accounts for as a plant

definitions.meaning: the carnivorous plant catches insects, so it causes the loss of bugs
a bristly plant of the borage family

explanation.surface: A Venus flytrap's insect catch is described as being a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, BUG LOSS, for the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugloss is a bristly herb related to borage; the flytrap accounts for many insects lost.

clue.text: Brat's piety seems phony in sacred area

indicators.note: something phony is fake, so the letters are rearranged into a false form

explanation.surface: A naughty child's devotion looks fake in a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptistery is the part of a church set aside for christenings, so a holy space.

clue.text: It may contain bits for hedger and sand

definitions.text: It may contain bits for hedger and sand

indicators.note: the letters are broken into bits and reassembled to make something new

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the garden that might store a gardener's tools and some sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits for' rearranges HEDGER and SAND; the whole clue also describes the answer, a hut storing a gardener's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A small outbuilding in a garden is where trimmers, tools and bags of sand are stored.

clue.text: Black bishop in commercial activity

indicators.note: the abbreviation for bishop goes in the word for selling

parts.note: a sale is a commercial transaction
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A dark chess bishop placed among a market transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black bishop' suggests chess, but 'Black' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for the colour black.

clue.text: Said stitching was apparent

indicators.note: signals that the word for stitching is heard rather than seen

parts.note: seaming is joining with stitches

explanation.surface: Someone claimed the needlework was visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeming means outwardly appearing, as in a seeming contradiction.

clue.text: Minute swimming animal found by girl and dad

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A girl and her father discover a tiny creature swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A salp is a small transparent sea creature, a tunicate that floats in the ocean.

clue.text: River sailor crosses in the morning

indicators.note: the sailor's word goes across, that is around, the morning abbreviation

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A sailor crosses a river early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar forms most of the border between Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is a river in south-west England.

clue.text: Some celebration that never finishes

indicators.note: the celebration's word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: a party is a celebration

explanation.surface: A party that goes on for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Part means a portion, as in 'part of the cake' meaning some of it.

clue.text: Something hazy with colour not completely right

indicators.note: the colour word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: blue is a colour

explanation.surface: A vague shape whose colour is not quite correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is an indistinct shape seen without focus.

clue.text: Inclination to leap after end of exams

indicators.note: places the leaping word after the letter picked from exams
takes only the final letter of exams

parts.note: to lope is to move with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: A desire to jump about when the exams are over.
explanation.definitionFit: An incline or slant is a gradient, a sloping surface.

clue.text: Bird abandoning lake gets one gawking

indicators.note: the bird's name leaves the abbreviation for lake behind

parts.note: the starling is a common bird

explanation.surface: A bird leaves a lake and someone gapes at it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawk is to gape or gaze fixedly, as staring does.

clue.text: Queries about way to address a gentleman

indicators.note: suggests the letters of queries are moved about

explanation.surface: Questions arise over the right form of address for a gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Esq. after a man's surname on a letter is a polite courtesy title.

clue.text: Repeat gets well-educated learner put off

indicators.note: the learner's letter is put off, removed from the word

parts.note: literate means well-read or educated
L is the learner abbreviation, from L-plates on cars

explanation.surface: A scholarly person is said to deter a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' suggests discouraging the learner, but signals that L is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again, as with a step in a process.

clue.text: Aimed to vanquish despair

indicators.note: to vanquish is to defeat and break up, so the letters of despair are routed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone set out to overcome hopelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's sights on a goal, to have ambitions.

clue.text: Entire home needing sensitivity

parts.note: in means at home
tact is sensitivity in dealing with others

explanation.surface: A whole household requires delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left undamaged and whole is complete.

clue.text: Sample egg emerging from cooking device

indicators.note: the egg's letter comes out of the appliance word

parts.note: a toaster is a kitchen appliance
O resembles an egg in shape

explanation.surface: A sample of egg pops out of a kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion offered to try, a sample.

clue.text: Pound one's given to artist, money no longer acceptable

parts.note: L stands for libra, the pound sign
one is the Roman numeral I
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A pound is handed to a painter in currency no longer valid.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian lira was replaced by the euro in 2002, so it is no longer legal tender.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy's former currency was withdrawn when the euro arrived.

clue.text: Sweet enthusiast consumes fifty

indicators.note: the enthusiast word eats, or holds inside, the numeral

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A dessert lover eats fifty of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open tart, a dessert or pudding.

clue.text: At home I am getting one furniture item that's unique

parts.note: in means at home
I'm is the contraction of I am
one is the Roman numeral I
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone at home gains a one-of-a-kind piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be copied is matchless and one of a kind.

clue.text: Grass in which animal rolls over

indicators.note: rolling over turns the animal word upside down, read backwards in an across answer

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: Tall grass where an animal rolls about.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass growing in water or marshes.

clue.text: Memorial provided by most serious individual

parts.note: gravest means most serious
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A monument supplied by the most solemn person.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone over a burial is a monument recalling the dead.
